style_guide:
# Enterprise Customer Onboarding Kickoff

## Source-image note

The supplied preview set currently duplicates the Executive Business Review image set. Reuse only its visual family—midnight cover, white enterprise pages, royal-blue structure, teal positive emphasis, clean cards, and disciplined tables. Do not reuse the EBR page meanings, fictional account facts, usage results, value claims, testimonial, risks, roadmap, renewal offer, or commercial values. This written guide is the authority for onboarding content and deliberately distinguishes preset 31 from preset 30.

## Purpose

Create a joint kickoff that converts the signed scope and success promise into an executable onboarding plan. The deck aligns desired outcomes, stakeholder roles, solution and integration scope, workstreams, risks, milestones, governance, and activation criteria. It is not a retrospective EBR, sales close deck, or generic welcome presentation.

## Visual signature

Use one dark midnight cover followed by cool-white body pages. Royal blue organizes workstreams, ownership, and milestones; teal marks confirmed readiness or completed gates. Clean rounded cards, thin borders, compact tables, and neutral enterprise typography keep complex implementation information approachable.

## Layout

- Fixed 16:9 canvas with `100 px` side margins and a 12-column grid.
- Reserve `135–170 px` for eyebrow and conclusion-led headline.
- Use `5/7` outcome-and-stakeholder split, three scope columns, a workstream matrix, three risk rows, and a full-width milestone plan.
- Cards may use `8–12 px` radius and a subtle shadow; avoid dashboard clutter.
- Keep body pages at least 80 percent white or cool off-white.

## Colors

- Midnight `#101827`: cover and governance authority.
- Royal blue `#1762F2`: titles, workstreams, owner chips, milestone gates, and required actions.
- Teal `#13B985`: confirmed readiness, completed prerequisite, and accepted decision.
- White `#FFFFFF`: cards.
- Cool canvas `#F4F7FA`: body background.
- Ink `#111B31`: primary text.
- Slate `#53627A`: support.
- Rule `#DDE4EC`: borders.
- Amber and red are reserved for explicit dependency or risk severity and must include text labels.

## Typography

Use `Inter`, `Aptos`, `Arial`, or `Helvetica Neue`. Cover title `54–66 px`; body conclusion `34–44 px`; milestone value `38–50 px`; panel title `20–26 px`; body `13–17 px`; table and source `10–13 px`.

## Page archetypes

### 1. Cover and partnership context

Use the midnight cover, blue-to-teal accent rule, onboarding title, customer and provider, kickoff date, contracted program, executive sponsors, implementation leads, and target activation window. Avoid value claims not yet realized.

### 2. Outcomes, scope, and stakeholder alignment

Show agreed success outcomes with measurement owner and acceptance evidence, then a stakeholder map with sponsor, decision maker, workstream lead, contributor, and escalation path. Distinguish signed scope from discovery assumptions.

### 3. Solution, data, and integration scope

Use three columns or layers for business process, product configuration, and technical integration. Show in-scope and out-of-scope items, environments, data sources, security prerequisites, integration owners, and unresolved design decisions.

### 4. Workstreams and responsibilities

Use a workstream matrix covering discovery, configuration, integration, migration, enablement, validation, and change management as appropriate. For every workstream define customer owner, provider owner, inputs, outputs, acceptance criteria, and dependency.

### 5. Risks, prerequisites, and joint actions

Use three or four rows for risk or prerequisite, impact, owner pair, mitigation, due date, escalation trigger, and exit criterion. Keep product gaps, access, data quality, security, resourcing, and change adoption distinct.

### 6. Milestones, governance, and activation criteria

Build a dated plan from kickoff through design approval, build, test, training, go-live, hypercare, and handoff. State meeting cadence, decision forum, status source, change control, activation criteria, and the first value review date.

## Onboarding integrity

Never invent contractual scope, customer readiness, access, data quality, security approval, stakeholder commitment, launch date, product capability, or resource allocation. Reconcile milestones with the statement of work and owner calendars. Label proposed dates until both sides confirm them. Every readiness state needs objective evidence. Keep future value as a target, not a realized outcome.

## Avoid

Do not reuse the duplicated preview's EBR facts or renewal narrative. Do not show usage or ROI as achieved at kickoff. Do not omit customer responsibilities, security gates, acceptance criteria, or change control. Do not call a dependency green merely because a meeting is scheduled.
